lines.text: This is Meridian, by Minor Hotels. A unified platform connecting every property, owner, and operating partner through a single surface and a single identity. One entry point to everything Minor Hotels offers. Built mobile-first, built for growth.

Start with the scale. Over five hundred and ninety hotels, across six continents and sixty-three countries, with a target of one thousand properties by twenty twenty-nine, eighty percent of it asset-light. Meridian is the technology condition that makes that growth executable.

That ambition exposes a gap. Three separate vectors, guest communication, workflow, and franchise enablement, are each arriving independently at the same missing layer, the operator surface that ties them together.

Vector one, the guest layer, is already a category. Canary Technologies runs in twenty thousand hotels. Duve handles over a million guest messages a month. HiJiffy, twenty-five hundred hotels. Meridian introduces the operational back-end to a program already in flight.

Vector two, workforce and task management. Minor's current stack, MessageBox, HubOS and Okami, works more like an audit log than a tool in the moment. HotSOS scales without a conversational surface, while ALICE and hotelkit are already moving from task lists to conversation.

Vector three, the franchise portal. Every operator answers differently. Marriott is spending one-point-one billion dollars. Accor failed twice before landing on D-Edge. And Wyndham invested three hundred and fifty million, earning ninety-six percent franchisee retention, by building around the franchisee's stack, not against it.

These aren't three products. They're three contexts, guest, workflow, and operation, bound into one surface. Conversational and agentic AI is the glue. One identity. One entry point. The home for AI. Only Minor owns all three.

Why now? McKinsey's research finds the real transformation isn't guest-facing chatbots, it's operations. And the pieces already exist. Leadership is aligned. A regional chief operating officer asked for this, unprompted. An internal agent, Tech Concierge, already runs on Minor's systems. And staff already ask ChatGPT when Minor's systems can't answer.

So what is it? Meridian is the intelligence layer above what Minor already has. The property systems, the P-M-S, revenue, and messaging, keep running exactly as they do today. Meridian is the common login and AI layer above them.

It delivers six service domains to every property: distribution, guest and loyalty, finance, workforce, development, and procurement. And it meets each property at the right depth, full integration for owned and managed, chosen integration for partners, and portal-first for franchise and affiliate.

The stacks differ by region, and that's fine. A staff member asking about a guest shouldn't need to know whether the record lives in the reservation system or the guest data platform. Conversational AI normalizes the chaos. Owners never see the stack, only the service.

On mobile, capability climbs in five tiers, from information and guest intelligence on day one, to property actions, live ancillary bookings, and full integration. Conversational AI runs through every tier.

Growth scales through one model, OMFA. Owned, managed, franchise, or affiliate. The relationship is the owner's choice, and Meridian meets each at the depth it justifies, deepening automatically as the relationship does.

No franchise deal is ever blocked by technology. Existing property system, Minor-provided, or none at all, Meridian handles all three, with conversational AI available from day one, regardless of integration depth.

For the partner, that means global distribution, Minor Discovery loyalty from day one, group-level guest intelligence the OTA will never have, portfolio benchmarking, brand standards delivered as workflows, and any stack, day one.

It changes how knowledge works. From a document that's filed and forgotten, to training content, to a live conversation, surfacing the moment staff ask, guiding the response, and logging the resolution.

One vendor is trying to become the whole platform. Mews raised three hundred million dollars, the largest hospitality software round ever, at a two-point-five billion valuation, and launched Mews Agent. But it's built property-first, with no franchise layer, no owner portal, and no multi-brand governance.

The approach is three phases. Alignment, a common language, with no technology yet. The unified portal, one surface, one identity, live from day one. And the full platform, where a guest message creates the task automatically. That last step is what Marriott is spending one-point-one billion to build.

The race is already underway. If Minor doesn't build this, someone else will sell it to its franchisees. Meridian is Minor Hotels' answer, built on what it already has, connected through a single surface, and designed to compound in value with every property that joins.
